title: Voice AI: STT, TTS and Voice Agents
brief: You are talking to a live voice agent right now. Let's pop open the hood and see how speech models hear, think, and talk back in real time.

questions.question: What are the three stages in a classic cascaded voice agent from the moment you speak to when it replies?
questions.answer: First, a speech-to-text model turns your spoken audio into plain written words. Next, a language model reads those words and writes back a helpful reply. Finally, a text-to-speech model reads that reply out loud as audio.
key_points: Speech-to-text turns your spoken audio into written words
A language model generates a written reply
Text-to-speech turns that written reply back into spoken audio
Written text acts as the handoff between each stage
questions.hint: Think of a three-person relay race passing a handwritten note from ears to brain to mouth.
questions.fun_fact: Most enterprise voice agents still use this three-step chain because engineers can swap any single stage or inspect the written log.

questions.question: In a live voice call, what job does voice activity detection do on the incoming microphone stream?
questions.answer: Voice activity detection listens to incoming audio and separates human speech from silence or background noise. It lets the agent trigger transcription only when someone talks instead of wasting work on dead air.
key_points: Distinguishes human speech from silence or background noise
Saves compute by only triggering downstream processing during speech
questions.hint: Picture a gatekeeper guarding the line who ignores room hum and quiet gaps until a person pipes up.
questions.fun_fact: In phone networks, this same speech detector powers silence suppression so calls do not waste data sending quiet pauses.

questions.question: How do modern neural text-to-speech models split the work between deciding how words should sound and generating the raw audio waveform?
questions.answer: First, one model turns text into rhythm, pitch, and compact sound features or audio tokens. Then, a neural vocoder or codec decoder converts that compact blueprint into a raw waveform. Splitting the job avoids predicting tens of thousands of raw audio samples directly from text.
key_points: One stage predicts pronunciation, prosody, or compact features and audio tokens from text
A second stage like a vocoder or codec decoder builds the raw audio waveform
Splitting the task avoids predicting thousands of raw waveform samples directly from text
questions.hint: Think of a composer writing sheet music before a musician performs every vibration on a real instrument.
questions.fun_fact: Kyutai's Mimi codec compresses spoken audio down to just 12.5 frames per second while keeping a voice crisp and natural.

questions.question: Why must a voice agent stream partial outputs across every stage instead of waiting for each model to finish completely?
questions.answer: Waiting for each stage to finish stacks up delays and creates awkward multi-second silences. Streaming sends partial transcripts, early reply words, and small audio chunks forward right away. That overlap slashes time to first audio so the agent starts talking in under a second.
key_points: Cuts perceived delay and time to first audio instead of stacking full delays from every stage
Overlaps speech recognition, reply generation, and audio synthesis in small chunks
questions.hint: Think of a kitchen serving each dish fresh from the stove rather than cooking a whole banquet before anyone eats.
questions.fun_fact: Across ten languages, humans leave an average gap of only 200 milliseconds between turns, so pauses past 600 milliseconds feel robotic.

questions.question: When you interrupt a voice agent mid-sentence, what must it cancel immediately and what must it fix in its conversation history?
questions.answer: First, the agent stops audio playback, clears queued sound buffers, and cancels ongoing text generation. Second, it trims the unsaid words out of conversation history so memory matches what you heard. Otherwise, the agent later refers to facts it generated but never actually spoke out loud.
key_points: Stops audio playback, flushes buffered audio, or cancels ongoing reply generation
Trims the unsaid portion from conversation history so memory only keeps what was actually spoken
Prevents the agent from referring later to things you never heard
questions.hint: Imagine a radio host cutting the broadcast mid-sentence and crossing the unread lines off their script.
questions.fun_fact: Smart interruption handlers also learn to ignore brief nods like uh-huh or yeah so polite listening noises do not cut the agent off.

questions.question: Why do fixed silence timers fail at conversational turn-taking, and how does semantic turn detection do better?
questions.answer: Short silence timers interrupt people pausing to think, while long timers make every reply feel sluggish. Semantic turn detection runs a small fast model to judge whether your words form a complete thought. It holds back after unfinished phrases like book a flight to, then answers quickly once you finish.
key_points: Fixed silence timers either cut off pauses mid-thought if too short or feel sluggish if too long
Semantic turn detection checks the meaning or grammar of what was said to predict if the turn is finished
A lightweight model inspects the partial transcript or audio cues in real time
questions.hint: Compare counting empty seconds on a stopwatch against listening to whether someone reached a period or a comma.
questions.fun_fact: Since planning a spoken reply takes our brain about 600 milliseconds, people start predicting when a partner will finish long before silence arrives.

questions.question: What goes wrong when a voice agent runs on open speakers without echo cancellation, and how does echo cancellation fix it?
questions.answer: Without echo cancellation, the microphone picks up the speaker output so the agent hears and interrupts itself. Echo cancellation uses the outgoing speaker audio as a reference signal to model how sound bounces back. It subtracts that predicted echo from the microphone feed, leaving behind only the human caller's voice.
key_points: The microphone captures the agent's own speaker audio, making the agent interrupt itself or treat its own voice as user speech
Echo cancellation uses the outgoing audio as a reference and subtracts the returning echo from the microphone signal
An adaptive filter keeps adjusting as sound bounces around the room differently
questions.hint: Think of a studio engineer who already owns the backing track and strips that exact melody out of a live recording.
questions.fun_fact: Even moving your coffee mug or leaning back in your chair changes how sound bounces off the desk, forcing the echo filter to retune on the fly.

questions.question: What do native speech-to-speech models gain over cascaded pipelines, and what engineering challenges get harder without an intermediate text layer?
questions.answer: Native speech models skip text conversion, cutting delay while keeping tone, emotion, and natural timing intact. Without a clean text middle layer, reliable tool calling, strict safety checks, and factual grounding get harder. Teams also lose an easy text audit trail, making bugs and policy slips much harder to trace.
key_points: Cuts latency or preserves vocal tone, emotion, and natural timing that written text loses
Makes tool calling, safety checks, factual grounding, or debugging and auditing harder without a text middle layer
Direct audio in and audio out removes the modular boundary where teams normally inspect or filter messages
questions.hint: Compare chatting face to face versus passing typed memos that a supervisor can review, stamp, and file.
questions.fun_fact: Kyutai's open-source Moshi model still predicts a silent inner monologue of text tokens alongside its speech so it stays smart while keeping latency near 200 milliseconds.
